user.title: Set up a heat pump
user.description: Wärmewacht only reads existing entities and never controls the heat pump. Templates found {found} heat pump(s); every entity can be changed in the next step.

data_description.name: Prefix of the entity ids.
data_description.source: A found heat pump fills in the entities; manual: pick them yourself.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description:
At least one mode needs a heat and an electricity meter, or at least the compressor (then cycling and electricity only, no ratios). Electricity meters of the compressor without backup heater; the backup heater separately.

Filled in by a template: the sections show what it found, the rest is under “More fields”. Leave a field empty rather than choose something similar; a wrong entity gives wrong figures.

heating.name: Heating
heating.description: The heat the heat pump produced and the electricity its compressor needed for it: cumulative meters in Wh/kWh/MWh, not power.

data_description.elec_heating: Electricity of the compressor for heating, without the backup heater.
data_description.aux_heating: Electricity of the backup heater for heating, if it is metered apart.

data_description.dhw_temp: Actual temperature in the hot water tank, not the setpoint. Gives charges and disinfections.

boiler.name: Boiler (hybrid system)
boiler.description: Only with a boiler next to the heat pump (e.g. hybrid manager HM200). Wärmewacht never counts the boiler as heat pump energy: its heat goes into heat load, energy signature and the heat pump's share. Best the heat the boiler reports itself; only without it the fuel (heat = fuel × boiler efficiency, settings).

data_description.boiler_heat_heating: Heat the boiler reports, with EMS-ESP usually …boiler_energy_heating_2 (Buderus “energy supplied”). Not …boiler_energy_heating without “_2”: EMS-ESP computes that one only from modulation × nominal power.
data_description.fuel_heating: Fuel of the boiler in kWh (EMS-ESP: boiler_gasmeterheat, in HA usually …boiler_gas_meter_heating, also for oil). Used for the heat only without a heat counter.

operation.name: Operation
operation.description: For starts, short runs, defrosts and standby.

data_description.compressor: An on/off entity, or a number above 0 while the compressor runs (speed, frequency, modulation in %). Not a status text such as "heating": that belongs under Activity.
data_description.activity: What the heat pump is doing (heating, hot water, defrost, ...), e.g. EMS-ESP "hpactivity". Gives defrosts and the mode of each run; without it runs are counted without a mode.
data_description.starts_total: The heat pump's own counter of compressor starts. Without it Wärmewacht counts starts from the setup on.

totals.name: One meter for all modes, special meters

data.heat_total: Heat produced total (meter, only without per mode)
data.elec_total: Compressor electricity total (only without per mode)
data.aux_total: Backup heater total (only without per mode)

totals.description: Only if the heat pump counts heat or electricity not per mode (then leave the fields per mode empty), or counts the electricity of defrosts and standby apart (Lambda, iDM).

data_description.heat_total: One heat meter for heating and hot water (e.g. between heat pump and buffer tank). Wärmewacht books it to the mode running; needs the activity for hot water. Then leave the heat per mode empty; cooling keeps a meter of its own.
data_description.elec_total: Only if the compressor electricity exists as one meter for all modes; then leave the fields per mode empty.
data_description.aux_total: Only if the backup heater exists as one meter for all modes; then leave the fields per mode empty.
data_description.elec_defrost: Only if the heat pump meters this electricity apart (Lambda, iDM).
data_description.elec_standby: Only if the heat pump meters this electricity apart (Lambda). Otherwise Wärmewacht separates standby itself.

data_description.outdoor_temp: Preferably the heat pump's own outdoor sensor; if it is in the sun, a nearby weather station.
data_description.flow_rate: Flow in the heating circuit (l/h, L/min, m³/h, ...).

activity_parts.name: Activity from several entities
activity_parts.description: Only if the heat pump has no single activity entity. An 'on' flag wins in this order: defrost, hot water, cooling, heating. The set mode turns heating into cooling while it cools.

more.name: More fields (not found by the template)
more.description: The template found nothing for these. Fill one in only if you are sure the entity delivers exactly this; one that only sounds alike gives wrong figures.

data.heat_total: Heat produced total (meter, only without per mode)
data.elec_total: Compressor electricity total (only without per mode)
data.aux_total: Backup heater total (only without per mode)

data_description.name: Prefix of the entity ids.
data_description.source: A found heat pump fills in the entities; manual: pick them yourself.

gas.title: Set up a gas boiler
gas.description: Before switching to a heat pump: heat load, heating limit and hot water share from the gas consumption of the last 365 days. Wärmewacht reads the long-term statistics of the counters, so a counter with a long history gives results at once. Choose either a total counter (heating and hot water) or a heating counter. No counter in Home Assistant? Choose "Readings by hand" and enter the meter reading now and then, weekly is best.

data.flow_in_circuit: Flow sensor sits in the heating circuit (after buffer or mixing valve)

data_description.gas_total: A gas meter (pulse, AI-on-the-edge) or the boiler's counter, in kWh or m³, with statistics. Hot water is estimated from summer days unless you choose a hot water counter.
data_description.gas_heating: Only if the boiler counts heating and hot water apart (e.g. Viessmann ViCare); then add the hot water counter as well. Leave "Gas total" empty.
data_description.gas_dhw: Optional: gas for hot water, if counted apart.
data_description.outdoor_temp: With long-term statistics (state class measurement). A nearby weather station is fine.
data_description.flow_temp: Optional: the flow temperature of the boiler or the heating circuit, with long-term statistics (state class measurement). Gives the flow at 0 °C and at the design temperature – what a heat pump would have to deliver at most. Only with a hot water counter, or with a heating counter if the boiler makes no hot water: a hot water charge lifts the flow. A sensor in the heating circuit needs neither (box below).
data_description.flow_in_circuit: Tick it when the sensor measures the flow of the heating circuit, not the boiler outlet (e.g. after a buffer tank or a mixing valve). Then hot water charges do not affect it, and the flow needs no hot water counter: Wärmewacht takes the hours in which the circuit runs (flow at least 25 °C, days below 15 °C), not the burner hours.
data_description.manual_unit: Instead of a counter: the unit of your gas meter. You enter its reading with the entity "Enter meter reading" or the action "Add meter reading (gas, oil)" (also for older readings, e.g. from bills). Each period between two readings of 5 to 35 days is one point of the energy signature.
data_description.calorific_value: Only for counters in m³: from the gas bill (kWh per m³, gross calorific value Hs).
data_description.z_number: Only for counters in m³: from the gas bill (Zustandszahl).

oil.title: Set up an oil boiler
oil.description: Before switching to a heat pump: heat load, heating limit and hot water share from the oil consumption of the last 365 days. Wärmewacht reads the long-term statistics of the counters, so a counter with a long history gives results at once. Choose either a total counter (heating and hot water) or a heating counter. No counter in Home Assistant? Choose "Readings by hand" (oil meter or tank level) and enter it now and then, weekly is best.

data.flow_in_circuit: Flow sensor sits in the heating circuit (after buffer or mixing valve)

data_description.gas_total: An oil meter in litres or a counter in kWh, e.g. the fuel counter of the boiler (EMS-ESP: boiler_gasmeterheat, in HA usually …boiler_gas_meter_heating, named so for oil as well), with statistics. Hot water is estimated from summer days unless you choose a hot water counter.
data_description.gas_heating: Only if the boiler counts heating and hot water apart; then add the hot water counter as well. Leave "Oil total" empty.
data_description.gas_dhw: Optional: oil for hot water, if counted apart (EMS-ESP: boiler_dhw_gasmeter, in HA usually …boiler_dhw_gas_meter).
data_description.outdoor_temp: With long-term statistics (state class measurement). A nearby weather station is fine.
data_description.flow_temp: Optional: the flow temperature of the boiler or the heating circuit, with long-term statistics (state class measurement). Gives the flow at 0 °C and at the design temperature – what a heat pump would have to deliver at most. Only with a hot water counter, or with a heating counter if the boiler makes no hot water: a hot water charge lifts the flow. A sensor in the heating circuit needs neither (box below).
data_description.flow_in_circuit: Tick it when the sensor measures the flow of the heating circuit, not the boiler outlet (e.g. after a buffer tank or a mixing valve). Then hot water charges do not affect it, and the flow needs no hot water counter: Wärmewacht takes the hours in which the circuit runs (flow at least 25 °C, days below 15 °C), not the burner hours.
data_description.manual_unit: Instead of a counter: an oil meter (litres, counts up), the tank level (litres, counts down) or a counter in kWh. You enter it with the entity "Enter meter reading" or "Enter tank level", or the action "Add meter reading (gas, oil)". With the tank level, after filling up first "Enter refill", then the new level. Each period between two readings of 5 to 35 days is one point of the energy signature.
data_description.boiler_type: Gives the efficiency on the gross calorific value: condensing 0.87, low temperature 0.79, constant temperature (mostly before 1990) 0.70, derived from the expenditure factors of DIN V 4701-10 (IWU 2005). The heat load changes in proportion.
data_description.boiler_efficiency: Only for "Custom value": the share of the oil that becomes heat, on the gross calorific value.

error.no_mode: Choose a heat and an electricity meter for at least one mode, or at least the compressor (then cycling and electricity only, no ratios).
error.energy_unit: An energy meter has no unit Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.aux_twice: Backup heater either per mode or as total, not both.
error.elec_twice: Compressor electricity either per mode or as total, not both.
error.heat_twice: Heat either per mode or as one meter for all modes (heat produced total), not both.
error.counter_twice: The same counter is in two fields (e.g. as heat and as electricity). Each counter belongs in exactly one field.
error.lifetime_counter: An energy meter rose on several days without starting anew: it looks like a total counter. This source delivers day values (energy today); choose those here. If it is a day counter after all, submit again unchanged.
error.day_counter: An energy meter fell back at the same time of day on several days: it looks like a day counter (energy today). Choose lifetime counters (total energy) here. If it is a total counter after all, submit again unchanged.
error.gas_none: Choose a gas counter (total, or heating) or readings by hand.
error.gas_manual_and_counter: Readings by hand need no counter and no flow temperature: leave those empty.
error.gas_twice: Either "Gas total" or "Gas heating only", not both.
error.gas_unit: A gas counter has no unit Wh, kWh, MWh or m³.
error.gas_no_statistics: A gas counter has no long-term statistics (state class total or total_increasing).
error.gas_calorific_value: Counters in m³ need the calorific value and the Z-number from the gas bill.
error.gas_flow_no_statistics: The flow temperature has no long-term statistics (state class measurement).
error.own_entity: A sensor of Wärmewacht itself is chosen as a source: the entry would read its own results. Choose the entities of the heat pump or the boiler.
error.boiler_without_heat_pump: The boiler needs the heat pump's heating meter (heat heating): its heat is compared with the heat pump's.
error.oil_none: Choose an oil counter (total, or heating) or readings by hand.
error.oil_twice: Either "Oil total" or "Oil heating only", not both.
error.oil_unit: A counter has no unit Wh, kWh, MWh or L.
error.oil_no_statistics: A counter has no long-term statistics (state class total or total_increasing).
error.tank_unit_change: Tank levels count down, meters count up: the readings entered so far do not fit the other kind. Keep the kind, or delete the entry and set it up again.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up. To change its entities, open it and use ⋮ → Reconfigure.
abort.gas_already_configured: This gas meter already has the entry "{title}". A second entry is not needed: add entities (flow temperature, hot water counter) there under ⋮ → Reconfigure, the design outdoor temperature and prices under the gear (Configure).
abort.oil_already_configured: This counter already has the entry "{title}". A second entry is not needed: add entities (flow temperature, hot water counter) there under ⋮ → Reconfigure, the design outdoor temperature and the price under the gear (Configure). Was it set up as a gas boiler? The fuel cannot be changed: delete that entry, then set up the oil boiler.

error.battery_both: Battery: please choose the charge and the discharge meter, or neither.
error.meter_unit: {entity} is no energy meter in Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.price_unit: {entity} reports its price in “{unit}”. Possible are {units}.

init.title: Settings

data_description.electricity_price: Gross price per kWh of the heat pump's electricity; empty: no costs. With a price sensor (under “More prices”): for the hours without its price.
data_description.design_outdoor_temp: From DIN/TS 12831-1 for your postcode (e.g. the BWP climate map). Without it the heat load is given per kelvin only.
data_description.boiler_efficiency: Only for boiler heat from fuel: heat = fuel × efficiency, on the gross calorific value (Hs) as the boiler counts its fuel. 0.87: field value of condensing gas boilers (DBU 2004), taken over for oil; a boiler that runs short and in pieces in a hybrid system reaches less.

costs.name: More prices and gas comparison (optional)

data_description.electricity_price_entity: For a dynamic tariff (Tibber, Nordpool, EPEX Spot …) or a template: each hour is priced with the sensor's mean of that hour from the long-term statistics (needs state class measurement), also the look-back before the setup. Unit ct/kWh, €/kWh or €/MWh.
data_description.electricity_base_price: Only for a separate heat pump meter (heat pump tariff), gross per year. On the household meter leave it empty: that base price is paid anyway.
data_description.gas_price: Gross, per kWh on the gross calorific value (as on the gas bill). Boiler efficiency 0.87.
data_description.gas_base_price: Gross per year; spread over the days of a period.

costs.description: Every field may stay empty. Without an electricity price (fixed above or a sensor) there are no costs; without a gas price no gas comparison; without a base price only the working prices are compared.

pv.name: Own PV and battery in the costs (optional)

data.grid_import_entity: Grid import meter (own PV and battery)

data_description.grid_import_entity: Optional: the meter of the grid connection the heat pump is behind. With it, heat pump electricity from own PV or battery costs the feed-in tariff instead of the grid price (only the costs change, not the performance factors). Not for a separate heat pump tariff meter.
data_description.feed_in_entity: With feed-in and PV meters the heat pump gets the grid share of the whole house; without them the grid import goes to the heat pump first.
data_description.pv_entity: With a hybrid inverter: its AC output.
data_description.battery_charged_entity: Optional, only together with the discharge meter.
data_description.feed_in_tariff: What own electricity would have earned when fed in; empty: 0.

pv.description: Only the costs change, not the performance factors: heat pump electricity from own PV or battery costs the feed-in tariff instead of the grid price. The grid import meter switches it on.

heat_load.name: Heating power from the data sheet (optional)

data_description.rated_power_kw: From the data sheet; gives the power per heat load.
data_description.min_power_kw: From the data sheet; shows whether cycling in mild weather is to be expected.

limits.name: Limits and evaluation

data_description.min_electricity: Below it the ratio is unknown instead of a random value.
data_description.starts_per_day: Optional, e.g. for a heat pump that only switches on and off: more starts within the last 24 hours make cycling conspicuous. Empty: off.
data_description.aux_mild_from: Daily mean outdoor temperature from which the heat pump should heat alone.
data_description.efficiency_drop_percent: Drop of the heating ratio against the previous season at the same outdoor temperature; off again 5 points lower.
data_description.disinfection_temp: Hot water temperature from which a charge counts as thermal disinfection (DVGW W 551: 60 °C at the outlet; the storage sensor may read lower).
data_description.season_start_month: The current season is recomputed from the statistics.

limits.description: When a check counts as conspicuous, and how ratios and seasons are counted. The defaults fit most heat pumps; change them only if a check is too strict or too lax for yours.

pv.name: Own PV and battery in the costs (optional)

data.grid_import_entity: Grid import meter (own PV and battery)

data_description.grid_import_entity: Optional: the meter of the grid connection the heat pump is behind. With it, heat pump electricity from own PV or battery costs the feed-in tariff instead of the grid price (only the costs change, not the performance factors). Not for a separate heat pump tariff meter.
data_description.feed_in_entity: With feed-in and PV meters the heat pump gets the grid share of the whole house; without them the grid import goes to the heat pump first.
data_description.pv_entity: With a hybrid inverter: its AC output.
data_description.battery_charged_entity: Optional, only together with the discharge meter.
data_description.feed_in_tariff: What own electricity would have earned when fed in; empty: 0.

pv.description:
Only the costs change, not the performance factors: heat pump electricity from own PV or battery costs the feed-in tariff instead of the grid price. The grid import meter switches it on.

Tip: if you also use [Tarifwacht]({tarifwacht_url}) or [Einspeisewacht]({einspeisewacht_url}), these fields are filled in already.

heat_load.name: Heating power from the data sheet (optional)

data_description.rated_power_kw: From the data sheet; gives the power per heat load.
data_description.min_power_kw: From the data sheet; shows whether cycling in mild weather is to be expected.

limits.name: Limits and evaluation

data_description.min_electricity: Below it the ratio is unknown instead of a random value.
data_description.starts_per_day: Optional, e.g. for a heat pump that only switches on and off: more starts within the last 24 hours make cycling conspicuous. Empty: off.
data_description.aux_mild_from: Daily mean outdoor temperature from which the heat pump should heat alone.
data_description.efficiency_drop_percent: Drop of the heating ratio against the previous season at the same outdoor temperature; off again 5 points lower.
data_description.disinfection_temp: Hot water temperature from which a charge counts as thermal disinfection (DVGW W 551: 60 °C at the outlet; the storage sensor may read lower).
data_description.season_start_month: The current season is recomputed from the statistics.

limits.description: When a check counts as conspicuous, and how ratios and seasons are counted. The defaults fit most heat pumps; change them only if a check is too strict or too lax for yours.

{summary}

Meters and sensors are not changed here: swap, add or remove them on the entry under ⋮ → Reconfigure.

oil.title: Settings
oil.description:
{summary}

Meters and sensors are not changed here: swap, add or remove them on the entry under ⋮ → Reconfigure.

data_description.boiler_type: Gives the efficiency on the gross calorific value: condensing 0.87, low temperature 0.79, constant temperature (mostly before 1990) 0.70, derived from the expenditure factors of DIN V 4701-10 (IWU 2005). The heat load changes in proportion.
data_description.kwh_per_litre: Gross calorific value of heating oil EL: 10.66 kWh/l (net 10 kWh/l after HeizkostenV, ratio 0.938 after the KfW/BAFA infosheet). Change it only if your dealer names another value.
data_description.boiler_efficiency: Only for "Custom value": the share of the oil that becomes heat, on the gross calorific value.
data_description.design_outdoor_temp: From DIN/TS 12831-1 for your postcode (e.g. the BWP climate map). Without it the heat load is given per kelvin only.
data_description.oil_price: Gross per 100 litres, as dealers quote it (e.g. for 3000 l).

start_after_end.message: The start must be before the end.

no_outdoor.message: This needs an outdoor temperature in the entities.

no_recorder.message: The report needs the recorder (long-term statistics).

no_look_back.message: This source has no usable statistics for a look-back.

look_back_failed.message: Reading the statistics failed; see the log.

reading_not_rising.message: The reading {value} does not fit: a meter only counts up, so it must lie between the readings before and after it.

reading_negative.message: A meter reading cannot be negative.

reading_in_future.message: The time of the reading lies in the future.

reading_not_found.message: There is no reading at this time (to the minute).

not_manual_gas.message: This entry is not a gas or oil boiler with readings by hand.

no_calorific_value.message: Readings in m³ need the calorific value and the Z-number (settings of the entry).

not_for_gas.message: This action is for heat pumps; a gas or oil boiler has the heat load only.

tank_rising.message: The tank levels do not fit the refills: a level lies more than 100 litres above what the earlier levels and the refills explain. A refill not entered? Enter the refill first (at a time before the level after it), then the level.

refill_not_positive.message: A refill needs more than 0 litres.

refill_not_found.message: There is no refill at this time (to the minute).

not_tank.message: This entry is not an oil boiler with the tank level read by hand.

missing_entity.title: Wärmewacht: entity missing
missing_entity.description: The heat pump {name} uses entities that no longer exist: {entities}. Renamed or removed? Choose them again under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

energy_unit.title: Wärmewacht: unusable unit
energy_unit.description: These energy meters of {name} report no unit Wh, kWh or MWh and are not counted: {entities}.

flow_implausible.title: Wärmewacht: flow rate implausible
flow_implausible.description: While heating yesterday, {entities} of {name} showed {measured} l/h on average; heat and spread give about {expected} l/h. Usually the unit is wrong (e.g. l/h reported as L/min) or it is the wrong sensor. Check the entity or choose another one under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure. The notice disappears after a day with a fitting flow rate.

flow_zero.title: Wärmewacht: flow rate 0 while heating
flow_zero.description: The flow rate of {name} ({entities}) stood at 0 for {minutes} minutes while the compressor was heating. A heat pump cannot heat without flow; usually the sensor delivers no real value. Check the entity or remove it under Reconfigure. The notice disappears as soon as flow returns.

lifetime_counter.title: Wärmewacht: total counter instead of day values
lifetime_counter.description: These energy meters of {name} rose on several of the last days without starting anew, like a total counter: {entities}. This source books day values (energy today); a total counter is counted with its whole value or not at all. Choose the matching day value under Reconfigure. If it is a day counter after all, ignore this notice.

day_counter.title: Wärmewacht: day counter instead of total
day_counter.description: These energy meters of {name} fell back at the same time of day on several days, like a day counter (energy today): {entities}. Wärmewacht counts them as lifetime counters and misses energy, on days below 1 kWh all of it. Choose the matching total counter under Reconfigure. If it is a total counter after all, ignore this notice.

energy_stale.title: Wärmewacht: no new energy values
energy_stale.description: For more than 30 hours the source of {name} has written no new hourly energy values ({entities}). With myVAILLANT (mypyllant) the energy is fetched only once at load unless the option 'Seconds between energy data updates' is set: set it to 3600 to 7200 seconds, or update one of its energy sensors with an automation. Wärmewacht catches up on the missing hours as soon as they arrive.

source_changed.title: Wärmewacht: energy entities changed meaning
source_changed.description: At least one energy entity of {name} no longer measures what it was chosen for ({entities}); with myVAILLANT this happens when the cloud reorders its energy series, for example after cooling was enabled. Wärmewacht books nothing until the entities are chosen again under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

activity_foreign.title: Wärmewacht: activity entity without an activity
activity_foreign.description: {entities} of {name} reports values that carry no activity on this device (for ViCare E3 controllers 'ready' / 'not_ready'). Defrosts and the mode of runs stay empty. Remove the entity under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

flow_return_swapped.title: Wärmewacht: flow and return swapped?
flow_return_swapped.description: While heating yesterday, the flow of {name} was {spread} K colder than the return on average: {entities}. A heat pump warms the water, so the flow must be warmer. Usually the two entities are swapped in Wärmewacht (Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure) or the sensors at the heat pump. A flow sensor behind a mixing valve can also cause this. Spread and flow temperature are wrong until then. The notice disappears after a day with a normal spread.

counter_stuck.title: Wärmewacht: meter stands still
counter_stuck.description: At {name} the compressor ran for {hours} hours, but these meters did not rise: {entities}. Wärmewacht books nothing meanwhile. Check whether the source (e.g. EMS-ESP) still sends values and whether the entity is enabled. If it is the wrong meter, choose another under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure. The notice disappears as soon as the meter rises again.

source_unavailable.title: Wärmewacht: source unreachable
source_unavailable.description: These entities of {name} have been unavailable for more than {minutes} minutes: {entities}. Meanwhile Wärmewacht lacks values. Check the source (e.g. EMS-ESP, MQTT or Bosch HomeCom). The notice disappears as soon as values arrive again.

outdoor_temp_stuck.title: Wärmewacht: outdoor temperature unusable
outdoor_temp_stuck.description: The outdoor temperature of {name} ({entities}) has not changed for {hours} hours. Performance curve, heat load and the checks 'Efficiency dropped' and 'Backup heater on mild days' depend on it. Check the sensor or choose another entity under Reconfigure.

outdoor_temp_implausible.title: Wärmewacht: outdoor temperature unusable
outdoor_temp_implausible.description: The outdoor temperature of {name} ({entities}) was outside -35 to +45 °C for {hours} hours yesterday. Performance curve, heat load and the checks 'Efficiency dropped' and 'Backup heater on mild days' depend on it. Check the sensor or choose another entity under Reconfigure.

own_entity.title: Wärmewacht: own sensor as a source
own_entity.description: The heat pump {name} uses sensors of Wärmewacht itself as a source: {entities}. It would read its own results, so they are ignored. Remove them under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure (leave the field empty or choose the heat pump's entity). Figures already booked from them stay.

report.name: Report
report.description: Heat, electricity and ratios of a period, also before the setup (from the long-term statistics), with months.

start.name: Start
start.description: Without: start of the current season. Times without zone are local time.

performance_curve.name: Performance curve
performance_curve.description: Ratio per 2-K class of the daily mean outdoor temperature, without standby (at least 7 days per class).

start.name: Start
start.description: Without: start of the current season. Do not mix seasons with different heating curves.

scope.name: Scope
scope.description: Heating, or heating and hot water.

heat_load.name: Heat load
heat_load.description: Energy signature: weekly heating power over the weekly mean outdoor temperature (weeks below 12 °C).

start.name: Start
start.description: Without: the window of the heat load sensors (the last complete season, without a usable one the current season so far; gas or oil boiler: the last 365 days).

end.name: End
end.description: Without: end of that window, or now with a start.

design_outdoor_temp.name: Design outdoor temperature
design_outdoor_temp.description: Without: the one from the settings.

config_entry.name: Gas or oil boiler

reading.name: Reading
reading.description: In the unit of the meter (m³, kWh or litres).

remove_gas_reading.name: Remove meter reading (gas, oil)
remove_gas_reading.description: Removes the reading at this time (to the minute), e.g. a typo.
